mission_01: A sample space is the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment. An event is a subset of the sample space. The probability of an event is the number of favorable outcomes divided by the total number of equally likely outcomes. The union of events uses the inclusion-exclusion principle: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). When events are mutually exclusive, P(A and B) = 0. Understanding sample spaces and events is the foundation of probability theory — every probability calculation starts by identifying the sample space and the events of interest.
